articles.title: Terrible idea or major coup? Galliano’s Zara collection launches after Met controversy
articles.summary: Collaboration regarded as ‘really big thing’ for retailer in some quarters despite backlash around designer’s antisemitic remarks in 2011. A month after it was announced that a planned exhibition dedicated to fashion designer John Galliano at New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art would not proceed…
body: Called Re{form}, it was, according to a press release, “authored by the couturier John Galliano. Built from our memory. Made for now.”

Its launch in shops comes after controversy over plans to honour the former Dior designer, who was found guilty of a hate crime in 2011 after a series of racist and antisemitic rants, with an exhibition of his work at the Met and a corresponding Met gala – a juggernaut of popular culture viewed by billions globally online. The exhibition was cancelled but had it gone ahead, it would have been only the third time such an honour had been bestowed on a living designer. The only others being Yves Saint Laurent in 1983 and Rei Kawakubo of Comme des Garçons in 2017.

The backlash to the plans were vehement and widespread, with Met patrons, New York politicians and prominent Jewish leaders objecting. Writing in the New York Times, his biographer Dana Thomas labelled it a “terrible idea”, saying that “choosing this moment to glorify the life’s work of someone who was convicted of making antisemitic remarks … is downright bizarre”, and noting that “his infamous antisemitic rants were not an aberration”.

articles.title: My wife obsessively consumes US news. She’s so stressed but can’t turn off. What should I do? | Leading questions
articles.summary: Instead of asking her to step away from her distress, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith, could you suggest she channel it into action? My wife is obsessed with everything that’s happening in the US.
body: I’ve told her she needs to take at least one day off all social media, but she won’t do that even for an hour. It stresses her out more and more every day, but she just keeps going back to it – and it has been really affecting me, more lately than ever. On weekends I stay up late playing games (my way of winding down after a week of work) and she’ll go to bed early. And during those times sometimes I just sit and cry. Everything that’s happening is so stressful, and there’s nothing we can do about it. I just wish I could rip away her phone and let her breathe! I don’t know what to say or do. Is there anything that could help?

Eleanor says: It’s so easy to feel that if you’re a politically engaged person you have to stay tuned in and upset. The general collapse of everything is distressing. So it can seem like an obligation of responsible citizenship to be distressed.
points: Instead of asking her to step away from her distress, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith, could you suggest she channel it into action?

articles.title: 'It’s a little splurge that adds a lot of joy': 22 whimsical products that make us smile
articles.summary: When life starts to feel boring, a touch of levity is just what the doctor ordered. Our contributors’ picks make even work and cleaning feel playful. A buckwheat pillow and 10lb blanket: what you loved most in September.
body: Welcome to Filter finds, a series where Filter contributors share the things they love most – and think you might, too.

The objects we choose to surround ourselves with should, above all, be useful – but life is short. Why not have a little fun while we’re at it? This month, we asked our contributors to share the practical things that spark not only joy, but whimsy – a sense of playfulness in our everyday lives. They certainly delivered!
From a toilet brush shaped like Excalibur to a concrete banana, these are the items our contributors use in pursuit of a whimsical life.

A couple in my town have installed some goose decoys in their front yard and dress them up thematically to delight passersby. And I am definitely delighted when I drive by and look to see what the “Nelsonville geese” are doing. They get dressed for holidays such as St Paddy’s Day, Cinco de Mayo (drinking Coronas), Fourth of July... and they have a Santa sleigh. They also do local things such as fishing in a baby pool to coincide with the local fish and game club’s fishing derby. They are hikers with trash strewn around their feet (a local peeve). During Covid, they social-distanced, 6ft apart.
points: When life starts to feel boring, a touch of levity is just what the doctor ordered.

articles.title: Peta claimed victory when fashion stopped using fur - so why are they back hijacking catwalks?
articles.summary: The animal welfare group has revived their runway-storming tactics from the naughts, now targeting the use of wool. Her walk was poised, her outfit – crop top, tailored trousers, high heels – so on point that when Josie Knowles strutted down a London Fashion Week catwalk last month she could have…
body: Still, as one social media commentator put it when praising her strut: “you cant tell me Peta didn’t know what they were doing when they hired this diva”.

The diva in question, Josie Knowles, 26, actually hired herself as part of her role leading fashion campaigns at Peta UK. Though she would not reveal how she got into last month’s H&M show (rumours of industry plants and sympathizers abound), she would confirm that dressing to “look the part” was part of her prep. For the record, Knowles’ clothes were all vegan and secondhand; the trousers were Spacegirlz, a now defunct early 2000s label; her high-heeled boots were from the Peta prop cupboard.

Knowles admits that she did practise her walk a bit (“I can’t say that I didn’t walk up and down my bedroom a few times”) but the main thing she practised was getting her sign out and unfolding it, because “obviously, for me, the most important part was getting my message seen, even if it would just be for a second”, she says.

articles.title: The 38 Best Restaurants in Mexico City, According to a Local Culinary Guide
articles.summary: The largest city in North America, Mexico City is a unique, elastic, ever-changing patchwork of food traditions. As a native of the city and a food writer covering the scene for the past 14 years, I’m still amazed by CDMX’s captivating energy and scale.
body: In the spirit of sorting out what is worth visiting, this list includes 38 restaurants and experiences for first-time and seasoned diners in Mexico City, focusing on projects that have distinctive culinary point of views, clear commitments to hospitality, and/or young local talent in the kitchen.

We update this list regularly to make sure it reflects the ever-changing Mexico City dining scene. Our write-ups include insider tips from our experienced writers and editors, as well as a rough range of pricing for each destination — ranging from $ for quick, inexpensive meals with dishes largely under $10 (or the equivalent in pesos), to $$$$ for places where entrees exceed $30.

New to the map in October 2026: Eater’s fall additions to the list move across neighborhoods and moods: A reinvention of one of Roma Norte’s favorites, Lalo, with an Italian-inspired new concept; El Distrito Fresco, a casual seafood spot fit for a long afternoon of eating and drinking in Tabacalera; an experimental bar, FO+MA, to end a night in Mexico City on a cocktail-heavy note; and Los Pacientes, a Doctores neighborhood taquería with a wide range of tacos and Norteño vibes.

articles.title: “Fresh and Youthful”: First Reactions to Kai Nesselrath’s Carven Debut
articles.summary: Industry insiders give their first impressions of Kai Nesselrath’s Carven, following his Thursday debut.
body: For his debut show at Carven, Kai Nesselrath dug into the archives, specifically the late ’50s and early ’60s, or “the peak of Carven” as he puts it. “I looked at these precise lines. And I come from a very tailored background — I wanted the collection to be very sculptural — so there are a lot of these lines in it,” Nesselrath said backstage.

Nesselrath started as Carven design director in June, succeeding Mark Thomas who exited the house in April. The new recruit joined from Saint Laurent, where he spent almost a decade rising the ranks to eventually become head designer of womenswear. Before this, the half German, half Italian designer, who is fluent in German, English, Spanish, Italian and French, also had a stint at Chanel.

But how does Nesselrath feel about being at the creative helm of a house? “ I’m enjoying it so much,” he said. “My best school was Saint Laurent. I met the best people there, who have been incredibly supportive. So I felt really sure about taking the job.”
points: Industry insiders give their first impressions of Kai Nesselrath’s Carven, following his Thursday debut.

articles.title: Where Was East of Eden Filmed? New Zealand Stands In for a Bygone California
articles.summary: The new Netflix adaptation of John Steinbeck's seminal novel was filmed in the same place as The Lord of the Rings and The Power of the Dog.
body: On Location peels back the curtain on some of your favorite films, television shows, and more. This time, we ask: where was East of Eden filmed?
Florence Pugh, who plays Cathy Ames, in a scene with Mike Faist as Charles Trask.

The answer turned out to be about as far from the US as one can get, on the South Island of New Zealand. Not exactly a novel filming location these days—the recent Heart of the Beast, and just about any movie by Kiwi Jane Campion has been shot there—one reason the place is so popular is that its vast, unspoiled terrain makes an easy stand-in for a bygone American West. Grant Major, the production designer for the series, says, “Generally, it's got mountains and snow and lakes and rivers and all that sort of stuff. We went there for The Lord of the Rings. I used the same farm that we used for East of Eden for The Power of the Dog.”
Below, Major takes us through shooting the project on location in his home country and tells us where, exactly, East of Eden was filmed.

articles.title: Shop John Galliano’s First Collection For Zara
articles.summary: The Spanish retailer Zara has signed John Galliano to a two-year creative partnership which will see him “re-author” the brand’s archives
body: The first collection from John Galliano’s collaboration with Zara is available to shop now worldwide at Zara.com. Featuring ready-to-wear including whimsical dresses, tailoring, and costume-like outerwea–plus an array of offbeat accessories. The collection marks the first of several over a two-year creative partnership. Below, read Nicole Phelps’s interview with the designer and shop the collection, now.

“I’ve been curating some of Zara’s recent archives,” Galliano told Vogue during Paris Fashion Week. “The idea is that I will re-author them.” The project came about via Galliano’s conversations with Marta Ortega Perez—the chair of Inditex, Zara’s parent company, and the daughter of Inditex founder Amancio Ortega. “I met Marta through MOP [the Marta Ortega Perez Foundation] and the wonderful exhibitions that she does—Steven Meisel, Irving Penn,” Galliano explained. (The MOP, established in 2022, presents photography and fashion exhibitions in A Coruña, Spain.) “Through those exhibitions, we started to strike up a friendship. I just like how open she is.”
